reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to confirm the refunds table matches what Alpha reported. I'll start by listing the refunds.
The refunds table matches exactly what Alpha reported: same three order IDs and amounts (121, 122, 124). Next I need the list of orders so I know which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly, so I can proceed. There are three customers in the orders (acme, birch, cobalt). I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 31368 cents. Acme's orders total 5706 + 25662 = 31368, with no refunds against them, so the figure checks out. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 14737 matches my check: orders 8002 + 13081 = 21083, minus refunds 5261 + 1085 = 6346. Next I need cobalt's net balance.
Cobalt's net balance of 24286 matches my check: orders 7562 + 22194 = 29756, minus refund 5470. All three balances reconcile, so I'll record the first payout, to acme for 31368 cents.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's balance of 14737 reconciles with orders minus refunds 121 and 124, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's balance of 24286 reconciles with orders 7562 + 22194 minus refund 5470, so I'll record its payout, the last of the three.
All three customers have been paid, and each payout matched its net balance. The refunds table matched Alpha's report before any payout was recorded.
